article.summary: Engraphis is a local-first memory system for coding agents. Its source describes a scoped SQLite store with temporal history, graph and vector retrieval, lexical search, and MCP or dashboard interfaces. This review records source behavior only; no local benchmark or runtime result was produced.

who_what.text: The official README presents Engraphis as local-first memory for coding agents, with a Python service, MCP server, and self-hosted web dashboard. The repository page identifies the canonical project as Coding-Dev-Tools/engraphis. The Atlas snapshot is used only to attribute the catalog locator, not as review evidence.

architecture.text: The SQLite schema models workspaces, repositories, sessions, and atomic memories. Memory rows carry workspace/repository/session identifiers, a scope (session, repo, workspace, or user), a memory type, text and summary, importance/confidence/stability fields, validity bounds, a recorded time for learned closure, and provenance metadata. The schema documents NumPy-backed portable vectors and an optional sqlite-vec backend behind a common vector interface; full-text indexing uses FTS5 when available and a plain-table fallback otherwise.

The recall module documents a pipeline of scope and time filtering, semantic-vector plus lexical plus graph candidate generation, reciprocal-rank fusion, retention-aware scoring, reranking, context packing, and reinforcement. The README describes retrieval as hybrid vector, lexical, graph, and code-aware search, with bounded context and citations or abstention when support is weak.

The README describes a local dashboard for graph/relation views, memory health, history, review, and operator controls. Source fields include access counts, last-access times, and temporal history; no live observability or resource use was measured in this review.

behavior.text: Write: the README documents a Python MemoryService.remember call and HTTP/MCP memory interfaces. It describes memories as typed and scoped. The schema includes provenance and confidence fields; the inspected review did not execute the service or verify end-to-end write persistence.

Update and correction: the README says the system preserves temporal history rather than silently overwriting. The schema stores valid_from, valid_to, and valid_to_recorded_at separately, and the mutation module includes closure-observation helpers. These source structures support temporal representation; they do not establish correction accuracy or stale-answer behavior at runtime.

Delete and erasure: the README documents memory/subject erasure and describes per-subject crypto-shredding while retaining an audit record. The inspected schema and mutation excerpts do not establish complete removal from every index, backup, sync peer, or derived artifact; erasure behavior was not exercised.

Retrieval: the code-level recall overview places scope/time filtering before hybrid candidate generation, then fuses, scores, reranks, and packs context. The README documents semantic, lexical, and graph retrieval with evidence citations and abstention. Candidate counts, recall quality, and calibrated abstention were not measured here.

Scope isolation: schema rows carry workspace, repository, session, and scope identifiers, and the recall pipeline begins with scope/time filtering. This establishes explicit scope fields and a source-visible filter stage, not adversarial or cross-tenant isolation; no isolation probe was run.

metrics.evidence: Hybrid retrieval and an abstention claim are documented, but this review ran no adjudicated recall or abstention probes.
Temporal validity and closure fields are present in source; correction accuracy and stale-answer rate were not probed.
The README describes subject erasure, but this review did not test deletion propagation or residual content across stores and backups.
Workspace, repository, session, and scope filters are source-visible; no cross-scope leakage test was run.
The README documents provenance and cited/abstaining responses; evidence precision and citation coverage were not adjudicated.
Vector, full-text, and graph retrieval paths are described; no latency distribution was measured.
No post-write recall schedule or availability probe was run.
Context packing and token-budget controls are described, but no workload token or provider-cost totals were collected.
SQLite, FTS, and vector storage structures are visible; no corpus storage measurements were collected.
Memory rows include access_count and last_access, and the README describes dashboard health and history views. Instrumented production telemetry was not inspected or measured.

limits.text: This is a bounded source review pinned to the verified main SHA. It did not run Engraphis, its test suite, or benchmarks. Source structure and README statements do not independently establish reliability, retrieval quality, authorization, complete erasure, or performance.

The pinned upstream README reports 71.1% lower mean retrieved top-5 context tokens (18 questions), a 54.71% lower serialized-JSON payload proxy (26 samples; 260 recalls), and 11/11 grounded decisions. These are upstream-reported fixture figures, not results independently reproduced or adjudicated in this review; benchmark_status remains not_run. Hosted services, local configuration, and end-to-end trust boundaries were outside the inspected evidence.
Contact check: the official pinned README was checked for a project contact email and none was found. No account/profile or commit metadata was used to infer one.

benchmark.text: Status: Benchmark not run for Engraphis in this project review. No system execution, tests, or benchmark workload was run; the project metric definitions and fixture describe measurement protocol, not Engraphis results.
